Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-21
Time: 10:00 PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Daniel Park (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood CSM), Maria Gomez (Acme ML), Tom Reynolds (Acme Infra), Ayesha Khan (Acme Product)

[00:00:05] Daniel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we've got about 45 minutes, main focus today is the cost/unit economics piece and follow-up from last week's benchmark, Priya will lead the numbers.
[00:00:18] Priya: yeah, hi all. Quick recap: we ran three model variants over the last 48 hours — base-7b fp16, quant-8b int8, and small-8b-qtz, and measured tokens per second and cost per 1M tokens. I uploaded the raw spreadsheet here: drive.google.com/drive/folders/example-benchmark (see sheet "week7-results").
[00:00:40] Maria: cool, let me jump in if that's ok, we care most about tokens per dollar at our tail latency target which is 150ms 95p for chat-style interactions. We had a couple of requests from product too about how caching would reduce spend for repeated prompts.
[00:00:54] Priya: right, so quick headline: quant-8b ran at ~420 tokens/sec on the dedicated rtx A10 pool we used, cost was approximately $0.018 per 1k tokens after reserved discounts — that maps to ~23k tokens/sec per dollar. The fp16 base-7b was faster in raw tps (about 480 tps) but cost higher per GPU hour, so tokens/sec per dollar was comparable, around 22k. The small-8b-qtz had lower latency for short sequences but hit worse unit economics once you factor in context growth.
[00:01:25] Tom: when you say reserved discounts, are those current Redwood Dedicated pricing or promo? I want to make sure our modelling matches enterprise commit levels.
[00:01:33] Daniel: good call — the sheet includes both on-demand and 1-year reserved assumptions. The numbers Priya quoted were for the 1-year commit at the mid tier. We'll share the pricing tiers in the follow-up.
[00:01:45] Ayesha: can you explain the tokens/sec per dollar metric in plain words — product wants something they can compare to their current hosted provider spend.
[00:01:52] Priya: sure — it's basically how many tokens produced by the model you get for each dollar of GPU cost. So higher is better; think of it as throughput normalized by cost. It helps you compare across model variants and infra configs.
[00:02:10] Maria: ok that helps. Did you run with KV cache enabled for the chat traces? that's where we expect to see the biggest wins.
[00:02:16] Priya: we did two runs with KV cache: one with small cache (32MB per session) and one with larger (128MB). Hit rates varied by persona — for customer support flows we saw 62% hit-rate on average, which reduced token generation by ~38% because repeated prefixes were served from cache. In cost terms that translated to roughly 30% savings on tokens/sec/$ for those flows.
[00:02:43] Maria: that sounds promising; is the hit-rate stable or did it degrade over longer sessions?
[00:02:47] Priya: it drops a bit for long conversations — after ~15 turns it went down to mid-40s% in our synthetic runs. There's tuning on session segmentation and cache windowing that can help. Also note our transcription had some mismatch where "KV cache" came out as "KV cash" in a couple of auto-logs, ignore that.
[00:03:02] Tom: latency impact from cache? did you measure tail P95 change?
[00:03:05] Priya: overall median latency improved by about 25ms for cache hits, P95 improved by 10-20ms depending on model variant. But if cache lookups are misconfigured you can see a small CPU overhead, so it's important to size the cache node and colocate.
[00:03:21] Liam: one operational note — for Dedicated we recommend dedicating a small sharded cache and monitoring hit-rate; we can provide dashboard widgets in Redwood Console.
[00:03:29] Daniel: let's talk batching — Priya you had a chart about micro-batching tradeoffs.
[00:03:33] Priya: yeah. We tested micro-batch sizes of 1, 4, 8, and 16. For latency-sensitive chat with tight SLOs, batch=1 or 4 gives best P95, but batching to 8 or 16 increases tokens/sec by 40-70% and improves tokens/sec/$ by almost 50% in some runs. The tradeoff is added queueing latency. For Acme's target of 150ms P95, we can probably push to batch=4 or 8 depending on request arrival patterns and if you accept occasional P95 spikes.
[00:04:05] Maria: do you have simulations for burst traffic? our traffic is spiky during product launches.
[00:04:10] Priya: we ran an arrival-model sim with bursts up to 3x baseline. Under those bursts, with batch=8 and dynamic autoscale, 95p latency stayed under 200ms but P99 spiked above 350ms. With batch=4 it was much more stable. So choice depends on how you prioritise cost vs worst-case latency.
[00:04:30] Tom: what about fallback model variants — e.g., route to smaller quant model during spikes to preserve SLOs?
[00:04:36] Priya: yes that's a pattern we recommend. Smart routing in Redwood can automatically fallback to compatible model variant (e.g., small-8b-qtz) for best-effort traffic while preserving priority routes for premium users. That also helps with unit economics.
[00:04:48] Ayesha: curious — how much complexity does that add operationally? our infra team is small.
[00:04:53] Daniel: Redwood handles most of the routing logic; we'll provide default policies and a canary config. Tom, we can also set up RBAC so your product team can't accidentally change routing for production.
[00:05:04] Maria: on the benchmark sheet, which workloads did you use — real production prompts or synthetic?
[00:05:09] Priya: a mix — we replayed a subset of anonymized production traces for chat, plus synthetic heavy-context scenarios. We note in the sheet which rows are replay vs synthetic. The production replay is most representative for cache savings.
[00:05:22] Maria: any surprising regressions we saw?
[00:05:25] Priya: only one: with quant-8b on A10s we saw slightly higher variance on long-context runs — likely due to kernel path for long KV lookups. We have an SE action to probe kernel selection and titrate sequence-chunking.
[00:05:39] Tom: can Redwood run an additional 24h benchmark with the cache + batch=4 recommended config and include cold-start impacts?
[00:05:46] Priya: yes we can. We'll also include per-route breakdown, and simulate 3x bursts. We'll push results to the same spreadsheet and flag new rows.
[00:05:56] Daniel: ok, plan for that. Next, cost projection — Daniel to run financial model for Dedicated commit vs Hosted pay-as-you-go given your 95th pct traffic projections.
[00:06:06] Daniel: I'll run three scenarios: low (30% commit), med (60%), high (100%) and include GPU hour pricing, k8s infra ops costs and data egress assumptions.
[00:06:15] Ayesha: do you factor in support and compliance add-ons? we need SOC2 and audit logs.
[00:06:20] Daniel: yes — pricing sheet includes optional compliance add-on and 24/7 SLA costs. We can separate those line items.
[00:06:27] Maria: a couple of product questions — does Redwood expose the cache hit-rate via API so we can do our own telemetry?
[00:06:33] Priya: yes, both Console metrics and an API endpoint; we can also push to your Prometheus if you want.
[00:06:38] Tom: regarding encryption keys — we'd use our KMS, right? how does Redwood integrate without the data plane seeing keys?
[00:06:45] Daniel: for Private/Dedicated we support customer-managed KMS and HSM; keys never leave your control. We'll share the security docs after the call.
[00:06:54] Maria: ok great. Any open risks we should surface?
[00:06:58] Priya: one risk is the long-context variance on quant models — mitigation is kernel tuning and maybe pinning to fp16 for the heaviest-context customers. Another is if cache hit-rates are lower than synthetic replay, savings will be less; we should instrument and run the 24h run to get production-like numbers.
[00:07:18] Ayesha: timeline check — we want a pilot decision by June 15, is that still realistic?
[00:07:23] Daniel: yes, with the additional 24h run and pricing follow-up, June 15 for pilot commit is attainable.
[00:07:29] Priya: ok I'll enumerate the exact runnable config: quant-8b with batch=4, KV cache 128MB/session sharded, autoscale min 2 replicas max 12, route fallback policy to small-8b-qtz for background traffic.
[00:07:44] Maria: sounds good. Please include expected cost delta vs current hosted provider in the sheet — our finance folks will want that.
[00:07:50] Daniel: will do.
[00:07:53] Tom: one quick ops ask — can Redwood provide a sampling of logs with the cache lookup timings so we can profile?
[00:07:59] Priya: yes we can provide p95/p99 cache lookup timings and an optional trace export. We'll redact user content.
[00:08:07] Liam: recap of next steps: Redwood to run 24h benchmark with recommended config, Priya to add cache hit projections, Daniel to send pricing and capacity scenarios, Acme to confirm SLOs and give feedback by 5/28.
[00:08:23] Ayesha: thanks all, that covers it.
[00:08:26] Daniel: thanks, we'll follow up in email and update the sheet.
